fixes.explanation: No feast is mentioned in this scene. Jonadab, Amnon's friend, asks, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?” That's all about Amnon being down, day after day. The text calls Jonadab a very shrewd man, so keep an eye on where this conversation goes.

Jonadab never mentions a doctor. He tells Amnon to say to his father, “Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.” The request is for Tamar to come and make the food. It begins with Amnon lying in bed and pretending to be ill.

Yes. King David sends word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.” That's his message to her, and it comes after Amnon asked the king for this while pretending to be ill. The text doesn't say more about what David knew, so I'll leave it there.
Yes. The text says, “So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.” That's where she is after Absalom speaks to her. I think this verse carries a lot of sorrow.

Adonijah isn't in this passage at all. The text says, “So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.” Absalom is the one who spoke to her after she went away crying aloud. I think this line is very sad.
